title: stream sentinel ordering and partial JSON reconstruction for SSE compatibility layer
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers and SDKs reported intermittent JSON parse errors and duplicate function-call events when using the OpenAI-compat streaming endpoint across unstable networks. Root cause analysis showed three related issues: (1) event delimiter heuristics relied on a strict "double-newline" boundary which could be split across TCP/chunk boundaries, producing empty events or merged tokens; (2) function-call/structured-output sentinels (short special markers inside data fields) could be cut mid-token and then re-emitted in a subsequent SSE event, resulting in partial JSON fragments that the client attempted to parse prematurely; (3) older clients that relied solely on delimiter-based reassembly made unsafe assumptions about event atomicity. Solution summary: introduce a compact stream-sentinel header and sequence scheme in the SSE event meta that is backwards-compatible and adds deterministic reassembly at the compatibility layer. Each SSE event now includes a small ASCII header line: "X-RW-SEQ:<seq_id>|<frag_index>|<total_frags>|<crc8>" (when fragmentation is possible). The compatibility layer uses these headers to: (a) buffer and reassemble partial data by seq_id, honoring frag_index ordering; (b) validate fragment integrity via crc8 and drop/mark corrupted fragments; (c) emit only fully reconstructed, canonical events to downstream SDKs; (d) preserve legacy delimiter behavior when header is absent so older clients continue to work. Implementation details: - Added stream-sentinel encoder/decoder in the compatibility proxy (pkg/sse/sentinel.go). The decoder maintains a small in-memory window keyed by seq_id and uses frag_index to detect reordering; out-of-window fragments are marked and logged. - For untrusted/large streams we cap reassembly buffer to 128kb per seq_id and a max 64 concurrently open seq_ids to bound memory. - Added crc8 checks for quick corruption detection; on mismatch the fragment is dropped and a lightweight diagnostic event is emitted (internal only). - Fixed edge-case where a trailing delimiter at chunk boundary created a zero-length event: explicit suppression for zero-length data unless a header indicates a true zero-length fragment. - Ensured that function-call sentinels are always reassembled before JSON parsing and added stricter parsing at the boundary for structured output to avoid early parse attempts. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for sentinel encoding/decoding and crc mismatches (tests/sse/sentinel_test.go). - Integration tests that replay recorded faulty chunk sequences from real incidents (tests/integration/sse/replays/) including replays that previously produced JSON parse exceptions. - End-to-end smoke tests with Python/TS SDKs to verify fallback behavior for clients that do not understand the header. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~0.2% median CPU overhead on the compatibility proxy under representative streaming workloads; memory bounding prevents OOM at scale. Rollout plan: canary to us-west-2 (5% traffic) for 24 hours, monitor parse-error-rate, client-latency histogram, and new debug metric rw.sse.reassembly_failures. If stable, ramp to 50% then 100% over 48 hours. If reassembly_failures exceed 0.1% or latency p99 increases >10%, automatic rollback to the previous proxy image will trigger. Migration notes: - No action required by customers. - SDKs updated to log and expose rw-seq metadata for advanced debugging (redwood-sdk-python v1.12.3, redwood-sdk-typescript v0.9.7). Related: fixes ENG-4582, addresses parts of ENG-4620. Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration replays added [x] canary plan documented [x] release notes included

review_comments: Ethan Rivera: Can we avoid allocating ephemeral buffers per-fragment? Consider using a pooled buffer for the 128kb window.
Maya Chen (author): Switched to sync.Pool-backed buffers for hot-path allocation in sentinel.go; benchmark shows reduced GC pressure.
Priya Kapoor: Add more conservative defaults for the reassembly limits in cloud-managed plans. Suggest lowering to 64kb for free-tier.
Maya Chen: Added plan-aware caps and feature flags; default remains 128kb for enterprise-managed proxies, 64kb for free/self-serve.
Noah Kim: Need a metric for dropped fragments and an automated debug dump endpoint guarded by feature flag.
Maya Chen: Added rw.sse.reassembly_drops and a gated debug dump at /_debug/sse/reassembly (requires admin token).
release_notes: Fix: SSE streaming compatibility layer now reassembles partial JSON fragments deterministically using a compact X-RW-SEQ header. Resolves intermittent JSON parse errors and duplicate function-call events for streaming clients. Backwards-compatible with older SDKs.
notes_for_ops: Canary 5% us-west-2 -> 50% -> 100%. Watch rw.sse.reassembly_failures, rw.sse.reassembly_drops, and parse-error-rate. Automatic rollback threshold: reassembly_failures > 0.1% or p99 latency +10%.
other_side_effects: SDKs bumped to expose seq metadata (python v1.12.3, ts v0.9.7). Minor CPU/memory overhead on proxy; bounded by per-seq caps.
